extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, patent examiners, and PTO staff
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory and PTO-directed standards governing patent fees, definitions, patentability (novelty/nonobviousness/subject matter), public access to PTO search systems, and formal application content. Applies to drafting, filing, and prosecuting U.S. patent applications and to fee/payment compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent search fee charging policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall charge the fees specified for the search of each application for a patent, except for provisional applications; the Director shall adjust fees to ensure that the fees recover an amount not to exceed the estimated average cost to the Office of searching applications for patent by Office personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority to set/search fees to match the Office's estimated average search cost; provisional applications are excluded. The Director must calibrate fees to cost-recovery (not exceed estimated average cost).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific patent search fee amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific fees: (i) $540 for each application for an original patent (except for design, plant, provisional, or international applications); (ii) $100 for each application for an original design patent; (iii) $330 for each application for an original plant patent; (iv) $540 for the national stage of each international application; (v) $540 for each application for the reissue of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory dollar amounts are the listed baseline search fees; applicability exceptions (design/plant/provisional/international) are spelled out. Director may adjust fees later under the fee-adjustment authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of existing fee-payment provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of paragraphs (3) and (4) of section 111(a) relating to the payment of the fee for filing the application shall apply to payment of the search fee with respect to an application filed under section 111(a). The provisions of section 371(d) relating to payment of the national fee shall apply to payment of the fee with respect to an international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment procedures and rules that apply to filing fees or national stage fees also govern payment of the search fees, per cross-reference to sections 111(a) and 371(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director authority to set other patent-related fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall establish fees for all other processing, services, or materials relating to patents not specified to recover the estimated average cost to the Office of such processing, services, or materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all authority to set cost-recovery fees for other PTO services; must be calibrated to estimated average cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified miscellaneous fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory specified fees include: $40 per property for recording a document affecting title; $0.25 per page for each photocopy; $3 for each black and white copy of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific transaction/service fees are statutorily listed examples of other fees the Director shall charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library copies yearly fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The yearly fee for providing a library with uncertified printed copies of the specifications and drawings for all patents in that year shall be $50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory nominal fee for libraries designated under section 12; applies annually for printed, uncertified copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of fees for government incidental requests and applicant notice copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may waive payment of any fee for any service or material related to patents in connection with an occasional or incidental request made by a department or agency of the Government. The Director may provide any applicant issued a notice under section 132 with a copy of the specifications and drawings for all patents referred to in that notice without charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretionary fee waivers for government incidental requests and free provision of cited patent specs/drawings to applicants who receive a section 132 notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual CPI-based fee adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees established in subsections (a) and (b) may be adjusted by the Director on October 1, 1992, and every year thereafter, to reflect any fluctuations during the previous 12 months in the Consumer Price Index, as determined by the Secretary of Labor. Changes of less than 1 percent may be ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic annual CPI adjustment mechanism; Director may ignore very small (under 1%) fluctuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity fee reductions and surcharges
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees charged under subsections (a), (b) and (d)(1) shall be reduced by 60 percent for any small business concern (per Small Business Act), and to any independent inventor or nonprofit organization as defined by PTO regulations. Any surcharge or fee charged under subsection (c) or (d) with respect to such entities shall not be higher than that required of any other entity under similar circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory 60% fee discount for qualified small entities/independent inventors/nonprofits; parity rule for surcharges so these entities are not charged higher surcharges than others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic-filing reduction for small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee charged under subsection (a)(1)(A) shall be reduced by 80 percent for any small-entity-qualified applicant if the application is filed by electronic means as prescribed by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhanced discount (80%) applies to the basic filing fee for eligible small entities filing electronically, incentivizing e-filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for false assertion of entitlement to fee reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity found to have falsely asserted entitlement to a fee reduction shall be subject to a fine, determined by the Director, of not less than three times the amount that the entity failed to pay as a result of the false assertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deterrent civil penalty (minimum treble amount of unpaid fee) for false fee-reduction claims; applies whether discovered before or after patent issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of public patent/trademark collections (no direct user fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall maintain, for use by the public, paper, microform or electronic collections of U.S. patents, foreign patent documents, and U.S. trademark registrations arranged to permit search and retrieval. The Director may not impose fees directly for the use of such collections, or for use of the public patent and trademark search rooms or libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public access to core PTO collections must be maintained without direct user fees; applies to physical and electronic collections and to public search facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated search systems deployment and public access
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall provide for full deployment of the PTO's automated search systems so they are available for use by the public and shall assure full access and dissemination of patent and trademark information using varied automated methods (including electronic bulletin boards and remote access).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation to make PTO automated search infrastructure broadly accessible, including remote and bulletin-board style dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access fees for automated search systems and limited free access
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may establish reasonable fees for public access to the PTO automated search systems. If such fees are established, a limited amount of free access shall be available for education and training. The Director may waive payment by an individual upon a showing of need or hardship, and if waiver is in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee authority is permitted but must include limited free access for educational/training purposes; Director has discretion to waive fees for hardship or public-interest reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report and comment opportunity on automated search systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall submit to Congress an annual report on the automated search systems of the PTO and public access thereto and shall publish the report in the Federal Register. The Director shall provide an opportunity for submission of comments by interested persons on each such report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency and stakeholder input requirement: annual public reporting plus comment opportunity on PTO search-system access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation and use limits for collected fees (PTO funding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees collected under this title shall be available to the Director to carry out PTO activities to the extent and in the amounts provided in advance in appropriations Acts. Any fees collected under this title and surcharges may only be used for Office expenses relating to processing patent applications and other activities, services, and materials relating to patents and to cover a proportionate share of administrative costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory restriction that fee collections be used only for PTO activities relating to patents (and proportionate admin costs); fees are not general Treasury revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent and Trademark Fee Reserve Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: There is established a Patent and Trademark Fee Reserve Fund: excess fee collections (fees collected in a fiscal year in excess of the amount appropriated to the Office for that fiscal year) shall be deposited in the Fund. Amounts in the Fund shall be made available until expended only for obligation and expenditure by the Office in accordance with appropriations Acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism to retain and use surplus PTO fee collections subject to appropriations; fund used to support Office obligations when authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director refund authority for mistaken or excess payments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may refund any fee paid by mistake or any amount paid in excess of that required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative authority to refund erroneous or excess payments voluntarily made to the PTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of Commerce annual reporting requirements to Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: On the day the President submits the annual budget, the Secretary of Commerce shall provide Congress's Judiciary Committees: (1) a list of PTO patent and trademark fee collections for the preceding fiscal year; (2) a list of PTO activities supported by patent/trademark fee expenditures and appropriations; (3) budget plans for significant programs/projects and out-year funding estimates; (4) any proposed disposition of surplus fees by the Office; and (5) such other information as the committees consider necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed, periodic financial and programmatic transparency obligations tying PTO fee collection/use to Congressional oversight and budget submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA first-inventor-to-file applicability and effective filing date rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The first-inventor-to-file provisions of the Leahy-Smith America Invents Act (AIA) apply to any application for patent and any patent issuing thereon that contains or contained at any time a claim to an invention that has an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013. Effective filing date is (A) the actual filing date of the patent or application containing the claim or (B) the filing date of the earliest application for which the patent or application is entitled to a right of priority or benefit under specified sections (e.g., 119, 120, 121, 365, 386).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines whether AIA/first-inventor-to-file rules apply by reference to claim effective filing date and priority/benefit chains; includes cross-references to statutory sections defining priority/benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (35 U.S.C. 100): key terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory definitions include: 'invention' (invention or discovery); 'process' (process, art, or method, including new use of known process, machine, manufacture, composition of matter, or material); 'United States' (USA, its territories and possessions); 'patentee' (patentee and successors in title); 'third-party requester' (person requesting ex parte reexamination who is not patent owner); 'inventor' (individual or individuals who invented or discovered the subject matter); 'joint inventor'/'coinventor' (one of the individuals who invented a joint invention); 'joint research agreement' (written contract/grant/cooperative agreement between 2+ persons/entities for experimental/developmental/research work); 'effective filing date' (actual filing date or earliest priority/benefit filing date as applicable); 'claimed invention' (subject matter defined by a claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory definitions govern interpretation throughout title 35 and are necessary to apply novelty, priority, and other patentability rules; note AIA applicability caveats for pre-AIA text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject matter (35 U.S.C. 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever invents or discovers any new and useful process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter, or any new and useful improvement thereof, may obtain a patent therefor, subject to the conditions and requirements of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory baseline for eligibility of subject matter to be patented; further limitations and case law may apply (AIA §33 references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty / prior art general rule (35 U.S.C. 102)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person shall be entitled to a patent unless the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, or in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General statutory bar to patentability based on prior art availability before the claim's effective filing date; effective filing date per 100(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year grace-period exceptions to prior art (102(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure made 1 year or less before the effective filing date shall not be prior art if (A) the disclosure was made by the inventor or obtained directly/indirectly from the inventor/joint inventor; or (B) the disclosed subject matter had previously been publicly disclosed by the inventor or someone who obtained it directly/indirectly from the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory one-year grace for inventor-originated disclosures and for certain derived disclosures; protects certain recent public disclosures by inventor from being prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions for disclosures appearing in applications and patents, and common ownership/joint research agreements (102(a)(2) and 102(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure shall not be prior art under subsection (a)(2) if (A) the subject matter was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor/joint inventor; (B) the subject matter had been publicly disclosed by the inventor (or someone who obtained it from the inventor) before the subject matter was effectively filed; or (C) the subject matter disclosed and the claimed invention were, not later than the effective filing date, owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person. Subject matter disclosed and a claimed invention are deemed to have been owned by the same person under a joint research agreement in effect on or before the effective filing date if the disclosed subject matter was developed and the claimed invention made by parties to the agreement, the invention was made as a result of activities within the scope of the agreement, and the patent application discloses or is amended to disclose the parties' names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory exclusions to treat certain prior art as non-preclusive where there is common ownership/derivation or joint research agreement relationship; requires disclosure/amendment to name parties for the JRA defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents and published applications effective filing-date rule (102(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: For determining whether a patent or application is prior art under subsection (a)(2), such patent/application shall be considered effectively filed as of its actual filing date, or if entitled to priority under specified sections, as of the filing date of the earliest such application that describes the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines the effective filing date of prior patents/applications for assessing prior art: either actual filing date or the earliest entitled priority/benefit date if such priority exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-obviousness standard (35 U.S.C. 103)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may not be obtained if the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art are such that the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious before the effective filing date to a person having ordinary skill in the art to which the claimed invention pertains. Patentability shall not be negated by the manner in which the invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conjunctive test comparing claimed invention as a whole to the prior art, judged by a PHOSITA standard; procedural and evidentiary considerations (e.g., secondary considerations) apply in PTO/ex parte practice and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biotechnological process special nonobviousness rule (35 U.S.C. 103(b) pre-AIA / exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon timely election by the applicant, a biotechnological process using or resulting in a composition of matter that is novel under section 102 and nonobvious under 103(a) shall be considered nonobvious if (A) claims to the process and the composition are contained in the same application or in separate applications having the same effective filing date; and (B) the composition and the process were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person at the time invented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special statutory protection for certain biotech process/composition claim sets allowing a process patent to be treated as nonobvious when tied to a novel composition owned by the same entity; includes rules for claim content and co-ownership, and special term synchronization rules for resulting patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ownership / joint research agreement exception under 103(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter developed by another person that qualifies as prior art only under certain subsections of 102 shall not preclude patentability where the subject matter and the claimed invention were, at the time the claimed invention was made, owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person. For this purpose, common ownership includes inventions made by parties to a joint research agreement in effect on or before the date the claimed invention was made, where the invention resulted from activities within the scope of the agreement and the application discloses the parties' names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallels the 102(c) common-ownership/JRA exceptions, applied in nonobviousness analysis to prevent certain otherwise-applicable prior art from negating patentability when ownership/assignment relationships or JRA conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions made/used/sold in outer space (35 U.S.C. 105)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any invention made, used, or sold in outer space on a space object or component under the jurisdiction or control of the United States shall be considered to be made, used or sold within the United States for purposes of this title, except where the space object/component is specifically identified/provided for by an international agreement to which the U.S. is a party, or is carried on the registry of a foreign state per the Convention on Registration of Objects Launched into Outer Space. If carried on a foreign registry, it shall be considered within the United States only if specifically agreed in an international agreement between the U.S. and the state of registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory rule treating U.S.-jurisdictional space activities as within the U.S. for patent law purposes, subject to international-agreement exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application formal requirements (35 U.S.C. 111)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for patent shall be made in writing to the Director and shall include a specification as prescribed by section 112 and a drawing as prescribed by section 113. (Applies to any patent application filed on or after December 18, 2013.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory baseline for application form and required contents: written application, specification (see 35 U.S.C. 112 for content/requirements), and required drawings (per 113). Cross-reference to pre-AIA/pre-PLT rules where applicable for earlier filings.
